method: NAIVE. Written straight from the deposited text using only the writing-l4-rules skill. No pipeline, no coverage table, no probe record, no independent test pass, no human gate. One pass, no review.
edition_encoded: Societies Act 1966 (Singapore), 2020 Revised Edition, informal consolidation in force from 1 November 2024, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/SA1966.txt. The deposit's arrangement of sections numbers Interpretation as s 3 while the body numbers it s 2; the encoding follows the body.

checks.command: l4 run sa-cases-registration.l4 ; l4 run sa-cases-unlawful-societies.l4 ; l4 run sa-cases-powers-procedure.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: THE WHOLE ACT bar s 3 (appointment of the Registrar), s 5 (the annual list), s 33A (amending the Schedule), s 34(1) (the regulation-making power) and s 38 (transitional). sa-registration.l4 carries s 2 (what a society is, with its exclusions, and 'officer'), the Schedule (the thirteen kinds of specified society), ss 4 and 4A (registration, the mandatory and discretionary grounds for refusal), the appeals to the Minister and which of them has a time limit, ss 6 and 7 (ceasing to exist and dissolving), s 8 (inspection), s 9 (branches), s 10 (information orders and their offences), ss 11 and 11A (changes of name and rules), s 12 (who may not act as an officer) and s 13 (insignia). sa-unlawful-societies.l4 carries ss 14 to 25: what makes a society unlawful, the nine offences and their penalties, which are deemed non-bailable, the presumptions in ss 21 and 22, triad rituals, ministerial dissolution under s 24 and the property consequences in s 25. sa-powers-procedure.l4 carries ss 26 to 37: entry, search and arrest, investigation and its offences, charging, composition, jurisdiction, forfeiture, service, the penalty for breaching regulations, the rules for a registered society's property, suits and dissolution, officers' liability for costs, and the power to exempt. No regulation, notification or exemption order under the Act was retrieved. The exemptions that ordinary social groups rely on in practice are therefore NOT represented, and no conclusion about whether a particular group is committing an offence can be drawn from this row without them.
